newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: FOCUS Czech cbank takes further step to ease crown grip.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS Czech cbank takes further step to ease crown grip.

text.p: The Czech National Bank (CNB) took its largest step yet toward easing its grip on the crown on Thursday, allowing banks to once again access its short-term last resort Lombard lending facility.
The CNB said it would open the facility, which was closed off in late May after the currency came under fierce pressure from a speculative wave of short-selling, from Friday at a rate of 50 percent.
"We are opening the Lombard credit facility from tomorrow," CNB spokesman Martin Svehla told Reuters. "The rate remains the same at 50 percent."
But Svehla said informal limits on non-residents' access to the Czech money market, agreed upon by the CNB and large domestic banks, remained in place.
Svehla said, however, the CNB's aim was to eventually open the money market again to non-resident investors.
"We have the intention, for sure (to remove the informal limits on non-residents), but I cannot specify now when and how we will do this."

The CNB has been loosening its tight grip on market liquidity in recent days, mainly through its repo rate, which has fallen from 75 percent to 31 percent. Before the crown crisis, the central bank repo rate stood at 12.9 percent.

The downward pressure eventually forced the CNB to allow the crown to float freely, after attempts to prop it up through a series of administrative measures such as the limits and interest rate hikes, and direct market intervention failed to deter speculators.
"As we move toward a more standard situation we will go gradually down with interest rates," Svehla said.
During the crown crisis, the CNB raised its discount rate to 13 percent from a previous 10.5 percent, and the Lombard rate to 50 percent from 14 percent.
The crown showed little immediate reaction to the move, trading at about 18.691 against the mark and 32.181 against the dollar in late Thursday activity.
Just before the announcement, the crown was at 32.186 to the dollar and 18.689 to the mark.
